title: Hybrid capacity-weighted geo-pin with tiered circuit-breakers and graceful shed
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a hybrid multi-region routing policy that combines latency-based routing with capacity-weighted geo-pin and a tiered circuit-breaker + load-shedding system. Goal: keep customer-facing p95/p99 latency SLOs stable during regional congestion or partial outages, while preserving error budgets and minimizing cross-region tail amplification.
background: We have recurring incidents where single-region hotspots or sudden capacity exhaustion cause cascading latency spikes when traffic is failovered unconditionally. Existing steering policies either prioritize latency (which can overload healthy regions) or capacity (which can cause long tail latency for pinned customers). We need a policy that balances: 1) stickiness to preferred region when healthy, 2) gradual failover under stress, 3) capacity-aware redistribution, 4) safety via circuit-breakers and staged shedding.
slo_targets: Error budget burn rate alert if > 10x over 30m
acceptance_criteria: Traffic routes follow geo-pin weights when regional health metrics are within SLOs
During a regional degradation, failover ramps traffic to other regions using capacity-weighted distribution within 60s instead of instant full redirect
Circuit-breaker opens for a region if p99 latency > 4x SLO or error rate > 3% for 5m, with exponential backoff retries
When global capacity utilization >= 85%, tiered shedding activates: low-priority routes shed first by X% then mid-priority, preserving 95% of critical requests
Dashboard shows per-region capacity, in-flight tokens, circuit-breaker state, and per-route bleed percentages
E2E chaos test injects increased latency in one region and demonstrates failover ramp + no SLO regression >5%
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Spec and config schema: define 'pin_weight', 'capacity_weight', 'circuit_breaker_thresholds', 'shedding_tiers' as first-class routing config
Phase 2: Router runtime changes: add capacity feedback loop that consumes GPU pool occupancy and inflight tokens from Dedicated/Private agents
Phase 3: Integrate SLO detectors: rolling p95/p99 and error rate windows feed into region health score (0-100)
Phase 4: Circuit-breaker controller: implement tiered open/half-open/closed with hysteresis and exponential backoff
Phase 5: Load-shedding controller: implement priority-tagged routes (critical, standard, best-effort) and progressive percentage shed rules
Phase 6: Observability & dashboards: add panels, alerts, and runbook links
Phase 7: Staged rollout behind feature flag with canary by customer tier
configuration_examples: shedding_tiers: [{tier: 'best-effort', priority: 3, shed_pct: 50}, {tier: 'standard', priority: 2, shed_pct: 20}, {tier: 'critical', priority: 1, shed_pct: 0}]
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Use a blended 'health score' combining p99 latency and capacity occupancy instead of hard boolean health checks. Rationale: smoother ramp decisions reduce oscillation and cascade failures.
Tradeoff: Introducing capacity-weighted routing increases cross-region traffic in steady-state compared to strict geo-pin; mitigated by pin_weight configurable per-customer.
Decision: Implement shedding at proxy layer to avoid queuing into backend GPUs. Rationale: dropping cheap requests early reduces downstream stalls and preserves capacity for critical traffic.
Tradeoff: Shedding low-priority traffic will increase client-level errors; must be surfaced in API response codes and billing logs to avoid confusion.
Decision: Circuit-breaker open condition uses p99 > 4x SLO OR error_rate > 3% sustained for 5m. Rationale: covers both latency and error storms.
Tradeoff: Conservative thresholds avoid flapping but may delay failover; mitigated by max_ramp_seconds and manual override flags.
Decision: Ramp windows default to 60s with configurable per-route overrides (fast-fail routes can be 10s).
observability: New metrics emitted: region.health_score, region.capacity_util_pct, region.circuit_breaker_state (0=closed,1=open,2=half-open), route.shed_pct
Alert: REGION_CIRCUIT_OPEN when circuit_breaker_state == 1 for >2m triggering a runbook
Dashboards: per-customer pin_weight vs actual routed_percentage, capacity headroom heatmap, cross-region tail amplification graph
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal traffic only (5% of internal prod) behind feature flag for 48h
Beta: 1% external traffic across low-risk customers for 72h, validate no SLO regression
Canary: 10% traffic across mixed regions, run chaos test (inject 150% CPU on one cluster)
Full: Gradual enable per-region over 7 days with automated rollback on SLO/regression alarms
Rollback: single toggle to disable capacity-weighted routing and revert to previous steering policy instantly
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for health_score calculation with synthetic latency and capacity inputs
Integration test harness simulating region failover with token-bucket throughput limits
Load test at scale: reproduce production 99th percentile behaviour using k6 + per-region worker pools
Chaos experiments: throttle network and inject GPU OOM in a region, ensure ramp and shedding behave as expected
E2E metric delta check: validate p95/p99 before and after during canary windows
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect pin_weight defaults causing excessive cross-region egress -> Mitigation: default conservative pin_weight=0.9 and customer-config override
Risk: Shedding rules impacting paid customers -> Mitigation: respect customer tier mapping and whitelist critical routes
Risk: Circuit-breaker flapping -> Mitigation: hysteresis + minimum open time + exponential backoff
Risk: Observability blind spots during rollout -> Mitigation: dedicated telemetry retention for canary windows and postmortem checklist
